---
title: "Start Here"
description: "The shortest path into a GeoEpi project."
---

If you are new to a project, start with its parent project in the GeoEpi Hub. The Hub is the place to understand why the project exists, who is involved, what data stewardship matters, and what the project is expected to produce.

1. Find the parent project in the GeoEpi Hub.
2. Read its objective, people, controlled-data information, deliverables, and current milestone.
3. Find or create the analytical subproject repository that matches your workstream.
4. Keep scientific implementation and reproducibility information in that repository.
5. Use Atlas or Ceres for approved large-data storage and computation.
6. Return accepted scientific outputs to project synthesis and products.

## The quick distinction

| Place | Use it for |
|---|---|
| GeoEpi Hub | Project context, coordination, decisions, people, milestones, products, and project-level data stewardship |
| Subproject repository | Code, documentation, analytical inputs, workflow entry points, provenance, and reproducible implementation |
| Atlas / Ceres | Approved controlled or large data, intermediate data, HPC execution, logs, temporary objects, and large outputs |
| Product or dissemination system | Manuscripts, reports, dashboards, released data, and related public or restricted outputs |

Continue to [How GeoEpi organizes work](../organization/index.qmd) when you need to decide where a project or subproject belongs.
